summary.text: A 20-year-old asymptomatic woman, G1P0 with a history of curettage, presented for termination of pregnancy 17 weeks and 2 days after her last menstrual period. Abdominal ultrasound showed a clear gestational sac, a fetus with heartbeat and placenta previa, with the sac at a distance from the uterine cavity and compressed myometrium between them.

MRI showed an enlarged uterus of 13.0 cm × 11.7 cm × 7.9 cm, a foetus with clear organs, a compressed lower uterine segment, and a gestational sac embedded in the right posterior myometrium and not connected with the cavity, with a linear hypointensity of the junction zone on T2 weighted imaging. The authors considered placenta implantation likely, and an intramural ectopic pregnancy in the second trimester was diagnosed.

Uterine artery embolization was judged inadvisable, and surgical exploration of the abdomen was undertaken under temporary balloon occlusion of the abdominal aorta placed just before the operation. The gestational sac was excluded and the uterus repaired by hysteroplasty without life-threatening haemorrhage and without uterine rupture. The postoperative course was uneventful, β-hCG fell to 1727 and then 440.1 mIU ml^(–1), and she was discharged 6 days after surgery.

evidence.quote: The uterus was also not ruptured.
her uterus did not rupture
As seen in our case, the uterus was as large as 17 weeks of gestation which probably resulted from uterine rupture, heavy bleeding and hypovolemic shock.

ambiguities.issue: The discussion says the 17-week uterine size "probably resulted from uterine rupture, heavy bleeding and hypovolemic shock"; this is hedged speculation (likely meaning what could have resulted), while the case text and introduction state the uterus was not ruptured and the sac was excluded without life-threatening haemorrhage. It is not treated as a source conflict and the rupture, bleeding and shock are not recorded as facts.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer uterine rupture, heavy bleeding or hypovolemic shock in this patient.

evidence.quote: showing an enlarged uterus of 13.0 cm ×11.7 cm × 7.9 cm, because of pieces of evidence

ambiguities.issue: The sentence giving the MRI uterine size ends in an unclear clause ("because of pieces of evidence") and does not say what the enlargement is attributed to.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer a cause of the uterine enlargement.

evidence.quote: clinicians excluded the gestational sac, repaired the uterus
Only three cases were confirmed by MRI in previous published reports similar to our report.

ambiguities.issue: The authors say the gestational sac was "excluded"; the extent of excision, histology of the specimen and the fate of the fetus are not stated. Cited published cases in the discussion belong to other patients and are not recorded.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer fetal demise, termination, pathology confirmation or a specific excision technique.

evidence.quote: Abdominal ultrasound revealed a clear gestational sac (GS), fetus with heartbeat and placenta previa.
This result is likely to be placenta implantation as the myometrium cannot be separated from the placenta.

ambiguities.issue: Placenta previa is stated as an abdominal ultrasound finding and placenta implantation is hedged as "likely"; the source does not say how the two relate or confirm either at surgery.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not treat placenta implantation as confirmed or equate it with placenta previa.

evidence.quote: If the area of the focal damage was heavy, the subtotal hysterectomy or hysterectomy was needed.
Otherwise, clinicians can perform excision by laparotomy and hysteroplasty.

ambiguities.issue: The hysterectomy is an if-then option worded "subtotal hysterectomy or hysterectomy", which asserts neither; the source states hysteroplasty was performed and never states that any hysterectomy took place.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not record a subtotal or total hysterectomy as performed or planned for this patient.
